2. Heard Sri. R.V.Shivananda Reddy, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri. K.Rahul Rai,
learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent-State.
Perused the materials on record.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner is the sole accused.
He is innocent and has not committed any offences as alleged.
He has been falsely implicated in the matter without any basis.
He was apprehended on 29.08.2022 and since then he is in judicial custody.
There is inordinate delay in lodging the first information.
There was quarrel between the petitioner and the family members of the informant in respect of financial matters.
Only to pressurize the petitioner, a false complaint was came to be filed.
The victim has not sustained any injury, which falsifies the contention that the petitioner has committed sexual assault.
The petitioner is not having any criminal antecedents.
The investigation is completed and the charge sheet is also filed.
Under such circumstances, detention of the petitioner in custody would amount to pre- trial punishment.
He is the permanent resident of the address mentioned in the cause-title to the petition and is ready and willing to abide by any of the conditions that would be imposed by this Court.
Hence, he prays to allow the petition.
4. Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader opposing the petition submitted that serious allegations are made against the petitioner for having committed the offence.
The victim herself lodged the first information making specific allegations against the petitioner.
Her statement under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., was recorded by the learned Magistrate.
She fully supported the case of the prosecution.
The statement of other material witnesses have been recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C.
After investigation, charge sheet is filed.
Considering the nature and seriousness of the offence and since the petitioner is the neighbour of the victim, he is not entitled for grant of bail.
Hence, he prays for dismissal of the petition.

5. In view of the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for both the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is:
"Whether the petitioner is entitled for grant of bail under Section 439 of Cr.P.C.?"

My answer to the above point is in 'Negative' for the following:

sentences.text: The allegations made against the petitioner are of serious nature.
The victim herself lodged the first information.
The date of incident is dated 25.08.2022.
However, the first information was came to be lodged on 28.08.2022.
Looking to the nature of the offence and age of the victim, the delay in lodging the complaint is not fatal to the case of the prosecution.
After investigation, charge sheet is filed.
Admittedly, the statement of the victim is recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., by the learned Magistrate, which is fully consistent with the first information.
The contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner that the informant has not sustained any injury is not a ground to reject the contention of the prosecution.
The informant is a married girl, aged 20 years, whereas, the petitioner is a young boy of 27 years who said to have committed sexual assault in the house of the informant.

Since there are strong prima-facie materials against the petitioner for having committed the offence, which are of serious nature, I am of the opinion that the petitioner is not entitled for grant of bail.
It is pertinent to note that the petitioner and victim are neighbours.
Under such circumstances, releasing the petitioner on bail itself may traumatize and prevent the victim from disposing before the Court.
Hence, I am of the opinion that the petitioner is not entitled to be enlarged on bail.

7. Accordingly, I answer the above point in the negative and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is dismissed.
At this stage, learned counsel for the petitioner seeks liberty in favour of the petitioner to move similar petition after examination of the material witnesses.
Learned HCGP submits that CWs.1, 4, 7 and 10 are material witnesses.
Liberty is reserved with the petitioner to move similar petition before the trial Court after examination of these material witnesses, if he is advised to do so.
